bars:Istioploikos.group: At the water and above it

old.name: Istioploikos
old.label: Mikrolimano
old.teaser: The yacht-basin sundowner: a two-level, ship-like deck set directly over the moored sailboats at the tip of Mikrolimano.
old.text: Mikrolimano is antiquity's Mounichia — the war-harbour of Themistoclean Athens — and its curved quay is now the city's yacht basin. Istioploikos ('the yachtsman'), named for the sailing-club tradition of the spot, has held the tip since 1997, a two-level deck that reads like a small liner ready to cast off. The café works all day from about 09:00; the kitchen and bar open around 21:45, and a DJ plays Sunday afternoons. The order is a chilled ouzo clouding over ice as the sun drops, and a whole grilled tsipoura or fangri eaten deck-side over the bobbing masts. Not a laptop table or a cheap round — a dressed-up sundowner at harbour-premium prices, recently relaunched after a full renovation.
extra: Signature: Cold ouzo and whole grilled fish, eaten over the moored sailboats at sunset.

bars:Horizon Rooftop of Senses.group: At the water and above it

old.name: Horizon Rooftop of Senses
old.label: Mikrolimano
old.teaser: Three staggered ship-decks stacked over Mikrolimano's fishing caiques, each level a different angle on the same Riviera horizon.
old.text: A hundred metres along the same fishing-harbour quay, at Akti Koumoundourou 24, the Horizon rooftop opened around 2022 and was built by designer Stratos Chiotellis to feel like a ship's deck — metallic arches and wooden decking, three staggered levels, the marina below standing in for the fourth wall (per LiFO, May 2026). It runs all day, 10:00 to 02:00, with weekend brunch — poached eggs on sando bread, pancakes, a club sandwich — before the evening turns to cocktails over the masts. Worth it for the deck and the sunset more than for destination mixology: a polished, see-and-be-seen rooftop at rooftop prices.
extra: Signature: An evening cocktail at golden hour, the glass sweating against the masts and open sea.

bars:801 Rooftop Bar.group: At the water and above it

old.name: 801 Rooftop Bar
old.label: Central Port
old.teaser: Eight floors up a converted Metaxa distillery — the one rooftop in Piraeus proper level with the cranes and departing ferries of the Great Harbour.
old.text: For eighty years this was the Metaxa distillery on the waterfront (1888–1968); converting it in 2024, Divercity Architects kept the geometry of the cognac barrels, so the building still carries the wooden arches and amber light of the spirit it once aged. The 801 sits on the 8th floor of the Mitsis N'U hotel at Aristidou 16–20, opposite Gate E7, and drinks eye-level with the busiest passenger port in Europe as the night ferries pull out below. The list leans on Greek spirits — the 'Liminality' builds reposado tequila and Metaxa 12 with chamomile, mustard seed and pink grapefruit; the 'Auteur's Colada' runs pandan, tsipouro, rum and coconut under Prosecco. Seasonal, late April to October, roughly 18:00 to 01:30 — the anti-Mikrolimano, the commercial port at industrial scale, and shut all winter.
extra: Signature: The 'Liminality' — reposado tequila and Metaxa 12, chamomile and grapefruit — as the night ferries pull out eight floors below.

old.name: Hams & Clams
old.label: Zea Marina
old.teaser: Piraeus's first oyster bar and its only Raisin-listed natural-wine address — French oysters and low-intervention pours on a Zea Marina deck.
old.text: It opened in 2016 as a 50 m² room and moved onto the Zea Marina deck at Pasalimani, where the calm inner bay and moored yachts read more Riviera than working harbour. The oysters fly in from France, opened to order with a bloody-Mary oyster shot to start; everything else — clam linguine, spicy tuna tartare, jamón ibérico and culatello sliced thin — comes off local boats. It is the single Piraeus entry on Raisin, the natural-wine directory, so the glass rides shotgun to the shellfish: ask what is open, since the growers are not published. Not a deep natural cellar and not a cheap round — a pricey marina raw bar on the port's most cosmopolitan stretch of water. A sister runs at Costa Navarino.
extra: Signature: Cold French oysters, a bloody-Mary shot and a natural glass, the marina rocking below.

old.name: Paléo
old.label: Retsina district
old.teaser: The deepest independent small-grower list in Piraeus, poured at near-retail markups you will not see at the marina.
old.text: The quarter is literally named Retsina — the port's old tobacco-warehouse zone, inland with no view — and Paléo lives inside one such warehouse on Polydeukous 39, the whole room built around the bottle. Sommelier-owner Yannis Kaimenakis travels the European South to unearth obscure small-winery labels — two to three hundred of them — and prices them near retail on principle, a quiet rebellion in a port full of markup. The by-the-glass pour changes as often as daily; put yourself in his hands, with a plate of pasta e fagioli or Tuscan chicken-liver pâté to hold the bottle company. Open Monday to Saturday 18:30 to 23:30, closed Sunday; Athinorama scores it 13.5/20. Opened April 2016 — a pilgrimage on an unglamorous industrial street.
extra: Signature: A daily by-the-glass pour of an obscure southern grower, chosen for you at the counter.

old.name: Méthe
old.label: Akti Miaouli
old.teaser: The port's newest wine room — a curious 40-label list reaching Austria and Georgia beside 48-hour Neapolitan pizza on the working quay.
old.text: Méthe — the Greek word for the euphoric drunkenness of wine — opened on 2 January 2026 at Akti Miaouli 73, directly opposite the blue-domed church of Agios Nikolaos, patron saint of sailors: a wine bar named for intoxication facing the sailors' church on the avenue where the ferries load. Chef Levis Kodimai works an open kitchen and a wood-fired oven, sending out 48-hour Neapolitan pizza, a Black Angus tartare with burnt-leek mayo, handmade rooster ravioli and a small cheese board with house jams. The list runs forty labels with eleven by the glass and a genuine reach — Austria and Georgia among them. Not a natural-only cellar, and Akti Miaouli is a workaday port avenue, not a scenic marina; Athinorama reviewed it on 26 January 2026.
extra: Signature: A 48-hour Neapolitan pie beside a chilled Austria or Georgia pour from the by-the-glass eleven.

old.name: Amsterdam Bar
old.label: Pasalimani
old.teaser: Pasalimani's rock room since 2008 — Bowie on the wall, bicycle-saddle stools on the marina sidewalk, a cocktail reliably poured to 05:00 on weekends.
old.text: Dimitris Doumakis opened it in 2008 as 'O'Canto', then renamed it Amsterdam to bring a bit of the Dutch capital to central Piraeus — Muppet Show memorabilia and a Bowie painting inside, bicycle-saddle stools on the Akti Moutsopoulou sidewalk facing Zea Marina, rock from pop to metal on the speakers. It runs daily 10:00 to 03:00 and to 05:00 on Fridays and Saturdays, pouring the house Zombie, a classic Margarita, whisky by the glass and cold draft. A solo drinker and a whole group both fit; it gets loud and busy at the weekend and keeps no kitchen — rock-led, not a tasting bar.
extra: Signature: A classic Margarita or the house Zombie, rock on the speakers, Zea Marina out front.

old.name: The Art of Bragi
old.label: Piraiki
old.teaser: The Piraiki's cocktail room since 2009 — cocktails told as stories, the sea coming in the open window, a signature still at eight euros.
old.text: Nikoletta Biza has run the bar on the western peninsula since December 2009, at Akti Themistokleous 154 on the wilder, unmarina'd edge of Piraeus. It takes its name from Bragi, the Norse god of poetry, and gives each drink a history: the 'White Zombie' pours white and agricole rum over Fassionola cordial, Caribbean pineapple and velvet falernum. Jazz, funk, soul and blues on the speakers, a whisky selection for neat drinkers, the sea breeze through thrown-open windows — a small, music-led drinking room with snacks rather than a kitchen, where the signature cocktails still land around eight euros.
extra: Signature: The 'White Zombie' — white and agricole rum, Fassionola cordial, pineapple and velvet falernum.

bars:Retsina — the port's wine.brief: From the old #drink prose (guide_text_old.txt, section [drink]): retsina, Savatiano with a splash of Roditis, Aleppo-pine resin in the ferment, a traditional appellation (OKP) not a PDO, the Mesogeia's white; barrel retsina at To Eidikon (its own table card: point to it, do not retell it). Labels: In the glass · On the label · Ask for. No place/Maps.

bars:Ouzo with the fried fish.brief: From the old #drink prose and the ouzo gem (guide_text_old.txt): ouzo (anise, the louche with water/ice, EU GI Greece & Cyprus), tsipouro, how the port orders it with fried small fish and mezedes, the karafaki. Labels: In the glass · On the label · Ask for. No Maps.

old.name: Rebetiko was born here
old.teaser: The port's founding sound — forged in the 1922 refugee slums, not in Athens.
old.text: Greece's urban blues took its shape in the tekedes — the hashish dens — of working-class Piraeus, in the quarters the 1922 refugees from Smyrna built at Agios Dionysios, Drapetsona and the Lemonadika fruit market on Karaiskaki Square. The bouzouki and the baglamas came ashore on the same quays as the ouzo and the meze; the Metaxas dictatorship outlawed the music and shut the dens in 1936, and it did not stop. UNESCO inscribed rebetiko in December 2017, its citation naming these Piraeus quarters as the ground it grew from.

old.name: The Famous Quartet of Piraeus — 1934
old.teaser: In 1934, four men in the hash-dens turned an outlaw's instrument into a national voice.
old.text: «Η τετράς η ξακουστή του Πειραιώς» formed in 1934 around Markos Vamvakaris, Giorgos Batis, Anestis Delias and Stratos Pagioumtzis — the first band built on the bouzouki and the baglamas, and the one that fixed the 'Piraeus style' until the Metaxas crackdown of 1937. Vamvakaris, the patriarch, left Syros for the port at twelve and learned the instrument in its tekedes; Pagioumtzis, a Smyrna refugee, provisioned the moored ships of the harbour by day before composers began writing for his voice. Vamvakaris cut «Φραγκοσυριανή» / Frangosyriani in 1935, the rebetiko that outlasted every other song from the tekedes.

old.name: Bayanteras — the one rebetis born in Piraeus
old.teaser: He named a song for the very back-street quarter where he was born.
old.text: Dimitris Gogos, 'Bayanteras' (1903–1985), was born at Vyronos 27 in the working-class quarter of Hatzikyriakio — the one giant of the Piraeus school who was a son of the port rather than a refugee or an islander come ashore. He took the nickname in 1925 after arranging Kálmán's operetta «Die Bajadère» for a bouzouki orchestra. His «Χατζηκυριάκειο» (1938) carries the name of his own street back into the songbook.

old.name: Revaizi — live in the birthplace quarter
old.teaser: The bouzouki still plays a few doors from where the Tetras took shape.
old.text: Agios Dionysios and Drapetsona are the refugee quarters where the tekedes stood; Revaizi, at Thermopylon 28 on that Drapetsona edge, is the mezedobouzoukleri still standing on the ground itself, a full kompania playing Friday, Saturday and Sunday. The kitchen is Cretan rather than Smyrnaic — chochlioi (snails) fried with rosemary, apaki risotto, raki — so come for the room and the raki as much as the songbook; it sits out toward Drapetsona, not walkable from the cruise gates.

old.name: The central rebetadika — Stou Thoma & To Palio Roloi
old.teaser: Where the neighbourhood, not the tour group, still breaks into song.
old.text: Two rooms in the centre keep the live tradition off the quay. Stou Thoma, at Mavromichali 22–24 in Agia Sophia, sits inside a stoa that was once the ticket entrance to an open-air cinema; the kompania plays Wednesday through Saturday from about ten. To Palio Roloi, at Dimosthenous 5 by the covered market in old Troumba — the sailors' quarter of Dassin's Never on Sunday — runs a Piraeus-blues band Friday and Saturday from around five, the zeibekiko danced by regulars. Both drift their hours; ring before you cross the port.

old.group: A rembetika kafeneio up the slope
old.name: Kafeniote
old.teaser: Wood-panelled rembetika room, owner-roasted raki, Sunday nights live.
old.text: Uphill on Leof. Vasileos Georgiou B' toward Kastella, at Mouson, a neo-traditional kafeneio-ouzeri that opens only in the evening. The owner roasts his own raki; the meze runs to smoked mullet under wood-panelling and warm lamplight, and on Sunday night the room turns to live rembetika. Get there early for a seat. Not a day-café or a work table — a smoky-warm room to sink into after dark.
old.meta: HOURS Wed–Thu 17:00–01:30 · Fri–Sun 17:00–02:00 · closed Mon–Tue · PRICE € (€5–10)

listening:Ta Paidia tou Pirea — 1960.group: The song the world knows, and the listening room

old.name: 'Ta Paidia tou Pirea' — 1960
old.teaser: Melina Mercouri sang Piraeus into an Academy Award, on these quays.
old.text: «Τα Παιδιά του Πειραιά», music by Manos Hadjidakis, sung by Melina Mercouri in Jules Dassin's «Ποτέ την Κυριακή / Never on Sunday», was set and filmed in the port in 1960. It won Best Original Song at the 33rd Academy Awards on 17 April 1961 — the first Oscar for a song from a foreign-language film, and still the only Greek song to take the prize. One detail gives the port away: the Greek lyric never once names Sunday; the English title was grafted on for the screen.

Search once or twice; if none, say plainly none found and point to the acoustic rebetiko rooms in this fold (the real listening in this port is unamplified). Never invent one. No Maps.
